title: playbook-consolidator-and-duplicate-step-clusterer
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Our runbooks/playbooks corpus has accumulated duplicated or near-duplicate remediation steps and fractured guidance across teams. This makes on-call work slower and increases drift in documented response. This PR introduces a Playbook Consolidator service and a duplicate-step clusterer that discovers semantically similar steps across the corpus and produces safe, reviewable consolidation suggestions. Approach: 1) Offline analysis uses sentence- and step-level embeddings (existing incident-bot embedding pipeline) with a two-stage clustering: approximate nearest neighbor kNN to collect candidates, then agglomerative clustering with a configurable similarity threshold. 2) Step normalization and canonicalization heuristics reduce noise (strip timestamps, redact instance IDs, normalize common command variants). 3) A preview-only consolidation patch generator emits a suggested merged playbook diff and a migration plan (backlinks from removed steps to canonical step ids). 4) Safety-first rollout: the consolidator runs as an opt-in job in the console and only produces suggestions; an operator can apply a dry-run patch or accept full migration. 5) UI: added a consolidation-preview page that surfaces clustering rationale, representative step samples, confidence scores, and links to related metrics (run count, last-used). Implementation highlights: - New package incident-bot/pkg/playbook/consolidator.go implementing the clustering pipeline and patch generator. - CLI: cmd/consolidate/main.go to run local analyses and produce JSON suggestions for manual review or automation. - Console: web/ui/playbooks/consolidation-preview.tsx adds an interactive diff + accept/reject flow (feature gated). - Telemetry: breath metrics (consolidation_runs_total, suggestions_generated, clusters_confirmed) and annotation of applied migrations for audit trails. Tests & validation: - Added unit tests for normalization rules and cluster scoring. - Small integration harness that runs on a 200-playbook sample (testdata/playbooks/dup_examples.yaml) to validate no-destructive merges. - Performance: approximate pipeline runs end-to-end on 200 playbooks in ~12s on CI runner with embedded caching; production job will be batched and rate-limited. Related work: references ENG-2134 (playbook hygiene initiative) and ENG-2199 (embedding infra stability). Rollout plan: feature-gated behind "consolidation" flag in console; initial run limited to internal sandboxes and docs teams, followed by opt-in org-level preview. Backout: generated patches are reversible; migration records are persisted for audit. Why different from earlier work: many previous PRs focused on incident snapshots, runbook generation, or triage helpers; this PR specifically targets long-term playbook corpus quality by recommending consolidation rather than auto-deleting content. Security & safety: redaction is conservative (requires manual review before applying), and all applied migrations are logged with user attribution. Docs: docs/playbook-consolidation.md explains the algorithm, UI flows, and suggested governance. Request: reviewers please validate clustering thresholds and canonicalization heuristics; UX reviewers please sanity-check the preview page.
